newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI units seen at PLN 168 at end 1996 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI units seen at PLN 168 at end 1996 - poll.

text.p: Polish brokers predict prices of mass privatisation NFI units will rise on the Warsaw bourse to 168.1 zlotys by the end of 1996, Nowa Europa financial newspaper said on Saturday.
The newspaper said the forecast, based on a monthly survey of Polish securities houses, was 37.2 percent higher than a month ago.
The units, which started bourse trade in-mid July and traded around 100 zlotys until late August, closed on Friday at an all-time high of 152 zlotys in record turnover.
Nowa Europa said the average forecast for the end of October was 162.8 zlotys and 175.7 zlotys for mid-1997.

The units have been on offer to Poland's 28 million adults since November 1995 at 20 zlotys each and will later be exchangeable for shares in each of the country's 15 National Investment Funds grouping more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
So far almost 19 million NFI units have been sold on the primary market, with the certificates on offer until late November this year.
The National Securities Depository (KDPW) has so far transformed about 5.2 million of the certificates into book-entry form, necessary for bourse trading.
